task.name: A diagnosis renders unverifiable claims and refuted claims identically, so a missing artifact reads as a completed check
task.story_text:
---
depends_on:
  - issue-2671
---

## Problem

A diagnosis presents every conclusion in the same voice. A claim checked against the
repository's source and a claim resting only on a snapshot someone else captured are
rendered identically, so the reader cannot tell which conclusions are load-bearing. When
part of the evidence is missing, the absence of a check reads as a completed check that
found nothing — and one earlier cross-project diagnosis retired a live hypothesis on
exactly that basis.

Depends on #2671: provenance can only be distinguished once a diagnosis has more than
one source to distinguish between.

## What

A diagnosis reports what each of its claims rests on, so an unverifiable claim is
visibly distinct from a refuted one.

## Acceptance criteria

- A diagnosis reports, for each claim it makes, whether the claim was verified against
  the target repository's source or rests only on attached evidence.
- Premise verification reports the premises it was unable to check, rather than emitting
  checked and unchecked premises in the same form.
- A claim whose supporting evidence is absent is reported as unverifiable. It is never
  reported as refuted, and never silently omitted.
- A diagnosis with no attached evidence reports every claim against a single source
  without introducing provenance noise into output that has only one provenance.

## Example

A diagnosis of a cross-project report, where the config snapshot is present but the
intake artifacts are not:

```
### Ruled out
- Layer-3 injection was inactive
  → refuted (verified: attached config snapshot records prior_run_context: true)
- The intake candidate was malformed at creation
  → unverifiable (intake candidate artifacts absent from bundle; not checked)

### Confirmed cause
- Router selected the fallback tier
  → verified against source (src/theforge/routing.py) and attached run log
```

The second line is the one that matters: today it would have read as a ruled-out
hypothesis, which is what turned a missing artifact into a false negative.

findings.description: A parsed diagnosis that omits claim_verification and confirmed_cause_verification is still treated as complete and renders without any claim-verification lines, so the landed diagnosis can present claims without saying whether they were checked against source or only attached evidence.

When a diagnosis carries attached cross-project evidence, premise verification is skipped entirely and the landed diagnosis contains no premise-verification section, so a diagnosis whose premises were never checked renders identically to one whose premises were all checked and found present.

When premise verification concludes a diagnosis is already resolved, the already-resolved report is rendered from the absent premises only, so premises the same pass was unable to check are dropped from the operator-facing output even though they were recorded in state and the audit.

The unable-to-check premises produced by verify_premise are covered only by unit tests on the verifier and on the markdown renderer; no test drives the diagnose flow end to end to confirm the values actually reach the artifact that is landed and the audit record that is written.

finding_registry.description: A parsed diagnosis that omits claim_verification and confirmed_cause_verification is still treated as complete and renders without any claim-verification lines, so the landed diagnosis can present claims without saying whether they were checked against source or only attached evidence.

When a diagnosis carries attached cross-project evidence, premise verification is skipped entirely and the landed diagnosis contains no premise-verification section, so a diagnosis whose premises were never checked renders identically to one whose premises were all checked and found present.

When premise verification concludes a diagnosis is already resolved, the already-resolved report is rendered from the absent premises only, so premises the same pass was unable to check are dropped from the operator-facing output even though they were recorded in state and the audit.

The unable-to-check premises produced by verify_premise are covered only by unit tests on the verifier and on the markdown renderer; no test drives the diagnose flow end to end to confirm the values actually reach the artifact that is landed and the audit record that is written.

A claim whose verification record carries free-text detail but an unrecognized verification type is normalized to the unknown type yet still counts as present for completeness, so the diagnosis lands as complete while rendering that claim as one whose source was never recorded.

On the attached-evidence path, the skipped-premise report is derived entirely from premise anchors and from file-like tokens parsed out of the affected code path, so a diagnosis that names its affected code in prose and supplies no anchors lands with no indication that the premise check was skipped at all.

When an attached-evidence diagnosis records no premise anchors and no file-shaped affected-code reference, the skipped-premise record is built with the entire free-text affected-code prose placed in the field that every other record uses for a repository path, and it is rendered inside code backticks and written to the audit under the same key.

soft: Coordinator is pure Python — no LLM calls for routing or process decisions
Schema validation is the integrity boundary — do not relax cross-validation rules

Keep modules single-purpose. Extract when a responsibility separates from its neighbours — never to satisfy a line count. Putting a change in an already-large module is correct if that is where it belongs; a module carved at whatever line got the count down is worse than the large module it came from.
Keep pure-data types in low-dependency modules with stdlib-only imports
Separate prompt construction, output parsing, and coordinator control flow

When adding or modifying data that flows between coordinator phases, instrument the change so the actual values are visible in the audit trail — diagnosing sprint failures requires tracing real data, not reconstructing it
Do not create files outside src/, tests/, or docs/. If you need a scratch file for exploration, delete it before committing.

Changes that affect coordinator phase boundaries, state handoff between phases, or adaptive routing/config propagation must include seam-level integration tests covering the touched boundary. Unit tests alone are insufficient when correctness depends on cross-phase state flow.
